name: Held v State of Montana
date: 14 August 2023 (first instance); upheld by the Montana Supreme Court on 18 December 2024

jurisdiction.court: Montana First Judicial District Court (Judge Kathy Seeley)

description: Petition by 16 young Montana plaintiffs against the State, concerning the provision of the Montana Environmental Policy Act (MEPA) that prevented agencies from considering climate effects in authorising fossil-fuel projects. The petitioners alleged violation of the Montana constitutional right to a “clean and healthful” environment (Article II, Section 3 and Article IX, Section 1 of the State Constitution).
outcome: Petition granted. The Court declared unconstitutional the provisions of the MEPA that prohibited consideration of greenhouse gas emissions and climate impacts, recognising a constitutional right to the climate as part of the right to a clean environment. The first case in the world in which a court has held a state law unconstitutional for preventing climate analysis in environmental authorisations. Upheld by the Montana Supreme Court in December 2024.
